import ctypes
import numpy as np

# Load the libraries
ctypes.CDLL('/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so', mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL('/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so')

# Define the gsl_function struct
class GSLFunction(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [('function', ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_double, ctypes.c_double)),
                ('params', ctypes.c_void_p)]

def gsl_integration_qk31(func, a, b):
    # Define the function prototype
    gsl.gsl_integration_qk31.argtypes = [ctypes.POINTER(GSLFunction), ctypes.c_double, ctypes.c_double,
                                         ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double), ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double),
                                         ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double), ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double)]

    # Prepare the function
    c_func = ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_double, ctypes.c_double)(func)
    gsl_func = GSLFunction(c_func, None)

    # Prepare the result variables
    result = ctypes.c_double()
    abserr = ctypes.c_double()
    resabs = ctypes.c_double()
    resasc = ctypes.c_double()

    # Call the GSL function
    gsl.gsl_integration_qk31(ctypes.byref(gsl_func), a, b,
                             ctypes.byref(result), ctypes.byref(abserr),
                             ctypes.byref(resabs), ctypes.byref(resasc))

    return result.value, abserr.value, resabs.value, resasc.value

def assert_test():
    # Define a simple test function
    def test_func(x):
        return np.sin(x)

    # Perform integration over [0, pi]
    result, abserr, resabs, resasc = gsl_integration_qk31(test_func, 0, np.pi)

    # Assert the result is close to the expected value
    assert np.isclose(result, 2.0, atol=1e-7), f"Expected 2.0, got {result}"
    assert abserr < 1e-7, f"Unexpectedly high error: {abserr}"
    assert resabs > 0, "resabs should be positive"
    assert resasc > 0, "resasc should be positive"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
